_comment: Shared spec for OtaCore.bundlesToPrune (Swift) / OtaCore.bundlesToPrune (Java) — F2, extracted from the boot-hook glue (OtaPlugin.java's runBootHook / OtaPlugin.swift's OtaBootHook.run) so the 'which bundle names need a prune pass after boot' decision is replayed by a shared vector file instead of living untested in native code. Deliberately NOT in the vectorFiles/VECTOR_FILES arrays the boot/confirm/loadFailed golden vectors use: this file has a different shape (state/shellName/expect.bundlesToPrune, no `op`, no `constants` block) and is replayed by its own loader/test function on each port (see OtaCoreTests.swift's testBundlesToPruneVectors, OtaCoreSelfTest.java's runBundlesToPruneVectors) — same convention as ota-prune-vectors.json. `expect.bundlesToPrune` is the SORTED union of active/pending/bootAttempts/confirmedBoots/rejected keys plus shellName itself. Both ports must produce byte-identical results on every scenario.

scenarios.name: bundle_only_in_bootAttempts_is_included
scenarios._comment: sub-a appears in NO map except bootAttempts — must still be returned, proving the bootAttempts union isn't skipped.

scenarios.name: bundle_only_in_confirmedBoots_is_included
scenarios._comment: sub-b appears in NO map except confirmedBoots — must still be returned, proving the confirmedBoots union isn't skipped.

scenarios.name: bundle_only_in_rejected_is_included
scenarios._comment: sub-c appears in NO map except rejected — must still be returned, proving the rejected union isn't skipped.

scenarios.name: shell_name_absent_from_every_map_is_still_included
scenarios._comment: `shell` appears in NONE of the state's maps (only `other` is active) — it must still be included, since a fresh device that has never staged anything but the embedded shell still needs its own prune pass.
